findings.title: Team admin check uses `&&` instead of `||`, blocking team admins who are not owners
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Because `isTeamOwner` only returns true for users with the `OWNER` role, using `&&` instead of `||` causes any team `ADMIN` who is not also an `OWNER` to fail the permission check and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when adding guests.

findings.title: `EventManager` is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` permits team admins/owners and attendees (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isAttendee`) to add guests, and fetches `booking.user` with `credentials` and `destinationCalendar` on lines 35-40. However, lines 158-165 initialize `EventManager` with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` instead of the booking organizer. When an attendee or a team admin/owner (who is not the organizer) adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` will run against the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's and fail to update the calendar event.

findings.title: Blacklist and existing-attendee checks are case-sensitive and `guests` is not deduplicated on the server
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` lowercases each configured address on line 71, but `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` on line 77 compares against the un-lowercased `guest` input, so any uppercase letter in a guest email bypasses the blacklist. Similarly, `guest === attendee.email` on line 76 is case-sensitive, and neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor `uniqueGuests` deduplicates the `guests` array itself, allowing duplicate attendee rows to be inserted if the endpoint is called directly with repeated emails.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives unfiltered `guests` and ignores disabled standard email settings
findings.body: Line 168 passes the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. If `guests` contains an email that already belonged to an existing attendee alongside a new guest email, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541`) will treat the existing attendee as a new guest and send them `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Additionally, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` like `sendLocationChangeEmails` and other functions in `email-manager.ts`.

findings.title: `isInvalidEmail` error state is not reset on valid submission or dialog close, and `onError` fallback is unreachable
findings.body: Once `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true`, it is only cleared when clicking the Cancel button. If the user fixes the invalid email and submits, or closes the dialog via Escape/outside click (`onOpenChange`) and reopens it, `isInvalidEmail` remains `true` and the error message stays displayed. Also, in `onError` (lines 43-44), `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is always a non-empty string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never be reached.
